fact: templates/, bin/, knowledge/, rubrics/ and guides/agent-coordination.md are mirrored into skills/ by lib/sync-resources.js and installed into user projects by /setup.
recommendation: Edit only the source, run `node lib/sync-resources.js --sync`; never hand-edit mirrors and never put metaswarm-internal content (e.g. this KB) in knowledge/ — use .beads/knowledge/.

fact: In Claude Code skill Bash calls PLUGIN_ROOT/CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT are usually unset, but the installed plugin's bin/ is on PATH; "${PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/x" becomes /bin/x and fails.
recommendation: Resolve plugin scripts with `command -v <script>` and fall back to ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-$PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/<script>.

fact: The npm/Codex installer (cli/metaswarm.js) symlinks skills/<dir> into ~/.agents/skills/metaswarm-<dir>, so a logical `cd ../../..` from an adapter lands outside the plugin.
recommendation: Use `cd -P`/`pwd -P` for relative plugin-root lookups from scripts under skills/, and warn (not silently skip) when a helper is not found.

fact: `bash tests/x/*.sh` runs only the first file (the rest become its arguments); and under `set -e -o pipefail` a no-match grep inside $(...) silently kills the script.
recommendation: Run suites with a loop (`for f in tests/*/test-*.sh; do bash "$f" || exit 1; done`) and guard greps in pipelines with `{ grep ... || true; }`.

fact: The Codex adapter reported the configured model in its JSON but never passed it to `codex exec` (no -m) — JSON-only tests could not catch it.
recommendation: Test adapter model passing with fake codex/gemini binaries on PATH that log argv; pass -m only when a model is configured so ~/.codex/config.toml still applies otherwise.

fact: Migrating a reviewer/output format by listing files in the DoD keeps missing copies: plan-gate rounds 3-5 of #54 each found one more old-format template (gate schemas, persona format pointer, agent 'exact format' template). Field-count wording is behavioural too: gate malformed-output rules key on 'lack the N fields', so stale '4 fields' would silently accept findings missing new fields (#58).
recommendation: Before migrating a format, grep every old-shape string repo-wide to inventory all copies, then add one permanent negative assertion over the whole file set (with named exclusions) instead of per-file DoD items. When changing a field count, sweep digit and word forms ('4 fields', 'four fields', '4-field') plus render placeholders (e.g. <finding>), and add them to the repo-wide guard.

fact: Digit-based sweeps (grep 'max 3|3 rounds|3 iterations') miss spelled-out counts such as 'after three rounds' or 'retry up to three times'; two survived into docs/index.html in #54.
recommendation: When sweeping for a removed number, include word forms (three|up to three|after three) and review docs/index.html prose by hand.

fact: agents/*.md and skills/start/agents/*.md are hand-maintained twins that intentionally differ in ./ path prefixes; separately, macOS awk mangles \( inside -v pattern strings.
recommendation: Test agent twins by asserting each clause is present in both copies, never by byte-compare; in awk -v regexes use . as a wildcard instead of escaped parens.

fact: In this repo every /metaswarm:* command and plugin Skill (e.g. plan-review-gate, orchestrated-execution) loads the installed plugin's cached release (e.g. 0.12.0), not the working tree; only unprefixed commands load working-tree copies from .claude/commands/.
recommendation: For a full working-tree dogfood run, start Claude Code with `claude --plugin-dir .` from the repo root, because reading skills/<name>/SKILL.md alone does not load working-tree agents: roleType() falls back to the installed metaswarm:<role> agents unless a current .claude/agents/metaswarm-<role>.md override exists. Check a Skill's 'Base directory' line to see which copy loaded.

fact: A project command file named after a Claude Code built-in (e.g. .claude/commands/status.md) shadows the built-in /status for anyone working in this repo.
recommendation: Keep built-in names out of the commands/ -> .claude/commands/ mirror (lib/sync-resources.js exclude list); tests/lib/test-sync-resources.sh asserts no mirrored command shadows a built-in.

fact: macOS git grep -E silently ignores \b (matches nothing), and grep -qF "--type decision" reads a pattern starting with -- as an option.
recommendation: In ERE use (^|[^[:alnum:]_]) / ([^[:alnum:]_]|$) for word boundaries and [|] for a literal pipe; always pass patterns with -e (grep -qF -e "$s").

fact: A RED check via `git stash` also stashes newly tracked test files, so the old tests run against the old files and pass; in zsh an unquoted $FILES list is not word-split, so `git stash push -- $FILES` stashes nothing.
recommendation: Stash only the non-test paths: write them to a file and use `git stash push --pathspec-from-file=<file>`, then run the new tests, then `git stash pop`.

fact: superpowers changes behaviour in patch releases: 7.0.1 started committing short design docs for small changes, while the local plugin cache held only 6.4.1 and 7.0.0. A claim that 'tested with X' was right for 7.0.0 would have been wrong.
recommendation: Before writing any superpowers version claim, fetch each tagged release with `gh api repos/obra/superpowers/contents/skills/<s>/SKILL.md?ref=vX.Y.Z --jq .content | base64 -d` and diff it. Don't rely on the local cache.

fact: Shell snippets in commands/*.md run in the user's shell, often zsh on macOS. zsh's default nomatch aborts the whole command when a glob such as docs/plans/*-design.md doesn't match, so a missing folder breaks the snippet.
recommendation: In documented snippets, don't use globs. Loop over the folders, skip absent ones with `[ -d "$d" ] || continue`, and run `find "$d" -maxdepth 1 -name '<pat>'` without `2>/dev/null` or `|| :`, so a read error on an existing folder fails loudly instead of silently falling back. Wrap the snippet in a subshell `( … )` and test it under bash and zsh, with and without `set -e; set -o pipefail`.

fact: `npx metaswarm install` does not exist: cli/metaswarm.js dispatches only init, setup, detect and --version, and anything else prints help. `setup` skips an instruction file that already mentions metaswarm, and /update only updates the marketplace plugin. Older docs still say `install`.
recommendation: Check command names and behaviour against cli/metaswarm.js (and commands/update.md) before documenting them, e.g. in CHANGELOG upgrade notes.

fact: Fixing a review blocker can introduce a new one. In #67, a fix to the upgrade note named a nonexistent CLI command, and a version boundary was stated one release late; each cost an extra review round.
recommendation: When a fix adds or changes a factual claim (a command name, version or behaviour), verify that claim against the code or upstream source before re-validating, not only the original finding.

fact: In macOS bash 3.2, when `set -u` aborts a script (e.g. "${ARR[@]}" on an empty array) and an EXIT trap is set, the script exits with the trap's status, usually 0. A test that crashes mid-run therefore looks like a pass to the enforcement loop. `set -e` failures keep their status.
recommendation: In test scripts with an EXIT trap, set DONE=0 first, have the trap end with `[ "$DONE" = 1 ] || exit 1`, and set DONE=1 just before the summary. Expand possibly-empty arrays as ${ARR[@]+"${ARR[@]}"}.

fact: Greptile applies the org's custom review directives as merge blockers: no magic numbers, no shared state between tests, stream instead of loading whole datasets, never swallow errors. On two consecutive PRs each one cost an extra fix-and-review round.
recommendation: Before opening a PR, check the diff against those directives. Use named constants, have each test build its own fixtures (own HOME and caches), stream large inputs, and give every fallback an explicit error path instead of `|| :` or `2>/dev/null`.

fact: On macOS, `iconv -f UTF-8 -t UTF-8 … >/dev/null` can print 'iconv(): Inappropriate ioctl for device' and exit 1 even for valid UTF-8 (seen with multi-KB input on macOS 15/26). With short input it may succeed, and after a real conversion error it can also report ENOTTY. So its exit code can't tell valid input from invalid when stdout is /dev/null.
recommendation: For UTF-8 validity checks in tests, use a node Buffer round-trip (`Buffer.from(b.toString('utf8'),'utf8').equals(b)`) instead of iconv to /dev/null. Don't dismiss an iconv failure as this quirk without checking the input.
